correctness.rationale: The involution orbit reduction is exact: all 256 words lie in 136 compatible internal orbits, all deletion outcomes are represented by 64-bit exact masks, and admissible strand-closed codes are exactly weighted cliques. Colored independent classes yield rigorous vertex-weight upper bounds; exhaustive include/exclude search returned max24 and 160 equality cases, and restriction to pair orbits max22 and 44 cases. Direct codeword shadow verification, complete inventory equality checks, fixed-word counts, and eight-permutation symmetry census all reproduced in bundled standard-library verify.py (VERIFY_OK, 104470/214187 and 4848/19219 states). No extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The finite Watson–Crick-closure plus one-deletion optimum and complete optimizer census are not logical corollaries of the inspected binary deletion, reverse-complement Hamming-separation, perfect different-radius or asymptotic quaternary indel results. Exact value, optimizer number and forced self-complementary minimum were compared against indexed scientific findings by parameter/statement and did not match. Historical-priority risk remains. García-Claro (2025) additionally covers linear codes invariant under reversal and complement separately and Hamming bounds, not the present nonlinear deletion graph.
residual_risks: A small-code table or older combinatorial design result not indexed by searched terms could imply the exact 24-word bound or the complete 160-codebook census.
There is no independent historical-priority audit; absence of a hit does not prove novelty.
Only the studied four-letter Watson–Crick closure model is evaluated; biological suitability and other channels remain untested.

value.rationale: The exact finite optimum for accommodating both DNA orientations while correcting one deletion is a natural constrained code size, and all equality cases are enumerated. A substantive structural boundary is proved: 24-word optimal codes necessarily contain self-complementary strands, whereas their exclusion sharply lowers capacity to 22; the 160-to-28 symmetry reduction further classifies the design space.
